correctness.rationale: For k≥1 positive planar fixed masses outside singular centers, Hess(m_j/r_j)=m_j/r_j³(3u_j u_j^T−I_2), with trace m_j/r_j³ because trace(u_j u_j^T)=1. For the stated rotating model ddot z+2J dot z=∇U, the standard KCC convention gives P=Hess U−I_2. The centrifugal quadratic contributes +I_2 and cancels, leaving sum of mass Hessians. Therefore tr P=Σ m_j/r_j³>0 for every nonsingular configuration, and real symmetric P has at least one positive real eigenvalue, violating strict KCC Jacobi stability along any regular trajectory. Direct independent matrix calculations for one and three noncollinear centers agree in trace and positivity. This is a correct elementary trace identity; it does NOT establish physical linear/orbital instability or apply at singular centers.
residual_risks: The earlier two-center KCC model has a physically self-consistent restricted system, whereas arbitrary fixed centers may not. This distinction does not introduce a new trace argument for the explicitly normalized mathematical ODE.
Jacobi instability is not Lyapunov instability, and collisions are excluded.
